title: Absolute ampleness after twisting a relatively ample invertible module
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume that $f$ is quasi-compact (the inverse image of each affine open is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), that $N|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, and that $M$ is ample on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there is an integer $a_0\geq0$ such that for every integer $a\geq a_0$, the invertible module $N\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z} f^*(M^{\otimes a})$ is ample on $Z$. Here $f^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the tensor products and tensor powers use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample), assertion (1); 'a >> 0' means every a beyond a bound.

proof.text: Use the existing generic theorem AlgebraicGeometry.bertiniTensorPullback_invertible from BertiniIncidenceNaturality for invertibility of tensor pullbacks; no incidence construction or incidence theorem is used. Identify tensor pullback with the usual pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints for the tensor-power and product comparisons. Quasi-compactness of T comes from ampleness and that of Z from quasi-compactness of f. For every affine V in T, relative ampleness and ample-implies-separated give separatedness of its preimage. Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.iff_of_iSup_eq_top applied to IsSeparated now proves f separated. Since T is separated, so is Z; in particular Z is quasi-separated. This replaces the former affine-intersection argument. Empty Z requires no separate branch.

At x choose m>0 and t in Gamma(T,M^m) with affine nonvanishing open V containing f(x). Pull the section back to q of B^m, B=f^*M, with locus U=f^-1(V). Relative ampleness gives n>0 and an affine section locus W on U containing x. Transfer the section through the pullback-power and restriction comparisons to s in Gamma(U,N^n). The restriction stalk isomorphism identifies nonvanishing of this ambient section at y in U with y in W.

Apply qcqs denominator clearing to L=B^m and F=N^n, obtaining e and a section tprime of F tensor L^e restricting to s tensor q^e. Multiply by q^b for b>0 and associate tensor powers. Its nonvanishing locus is W: the tensor locus formula gives the intersection of the locus of tprime with that of q. On U, q generates L locally by the nonvanishing/local-generation criterion, hence q^e generates L^e even for e=0. The residue-fibre tensor formula and restriction equation show that tprime is nonzero exactly where s is nonzero. Outside U the positive q^b factor vanishes. Use the proved pure-tensor and positive-power nonvanishing helpers from TensorSectionAffineOpen and NonvanishingCommonDegree.

For m dividing a and a>=m(e+1), set k=a/m and b=nk-e. Since n>0, b>0 and m(e+b)=an. Pullback-power and tensor-power isomorphisms carry the section just constructed to a section of (N tensor f^*(M^a))^n, still with locus W. Choose these W through all points; compactness gives a finite subcover indexed by a finite set S. Put D=product over S of m_i, E=sum over S of m_i(e_i+1), A=D(E+1). Then D>0, every m_i divides A, and every bound is <=E<A. The sections with fixed affine loci W_i prove P_A ample. The same formula works for empty S: D=1, E=0, and the pointwise assertion is vacuous.

The structure module is quasi-coherent and finite type: use the single generator of the free rank-one module, its isomorphism to the unit, and the local-generators data obtained by restricting this finite generating family. Eventual ample-twist global generation applied to O_T gives d; take K=d.toNat. For c>=K, transport the generating family along the left unitor to M^c. The nonvanishing-cover theorem gives a section nonzero at f(x), and the direct tensor-pullback fibre criterion gives a section of f^*(M^c) nonzero at x.

Prove that an ample invertible L tensored with an invertible P having nonvanishing sections through every point is ample: choose an affine section locus of L^n through x, and a section w of P nonvanishing at x. Tensor with w^n, then transport through tensorPowTensorObjIso. Its locus is the intersection of the affine open with the locus of w, affine by affine_cap_section_open, and contains x. Apply with L=P_A and P=f^*(M^c), c=a.toNat-A. The pullback tensor comparison identifies the result with P_(A+c)=P_a. The integer bound A+K is nonnegative, forces a>=0, and gives c>=K. Transport ampleness along this isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q60-d47b04f92 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks Tag 0892(1) and its proof (morphisms.tex 8829-8888). The item's statement matches it exactly: 'f-ample' means quasi-compact f plus ampleness over every affine open, and 'a>>0' becomes an a0 with all a>=a0. The delivery changes only proof, proof_deps, proof_origin, split_report and status; statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged and there are no new nodes. The item is live, unsplit and not dropped; no cited node is dropped or merged; there is no repair note. The dropped lem-per-relative-ample-absolute-twist has the same statement and is correctly not cited. I checked all 8 steps against the cited statements. Step 1: invertible-pullback-tensor (1),(2) give the power identities, Z is quasi-compact by permanence (2), and empty Z is handled. Steps 2-3: T and each Z_V are separated, and Z is quasi-separated through V''=V∩V' affine, quasi-compactness of U->V by permanence (1), and the affine-cover criterion (1),(2); no unproved hypothesis is used. Steps 4-5: the pullback nonvanishing locus Z_q=f^-1(T_t), then clearing denominators (01PW) on qcqs Z with F=N^n; the locus of s'q^b equals W by the fibre formula (3). Step 6: b=na/m-e>=1 and (e+b)m=na are verified, and A is a common multiple of the m_i with A>=1, so P_A is ample. Steps 7-8: global generation of M^c for c>=K (applied to O_T), a nonvanishing cover, u⊗w^r with affine locus via 01PV, and the iso to P_{A+c} via ample-iso, giving a0=A+K. Edge cases checked: empty Z or T, f=id, N=O with T not quasi-affine (A>=1), c=0, different m_i. rg -L finds no live duplicate: pbc-pullback-ample-invertible is 0892(2), the trf nodes are 01VJ and 0893. The declared off-unit tool_uses (generic scheme-theory lemmas, several of them Mathlib leaves or definitions) are accepted. No SGA source is used. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem isAmple_tensorPullback_tensorPow_of_relative {Z T : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ T) [QuasiCompact f] (N : Z.Modules) (M : T.Modules) [N.IsInvertible] [M.IsInvertible] (hN : ∀ V : T.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → ∃ h : ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj N).IsInvertible, @IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj N) h) (hM : IsAmple T M) : ∃ a₀ : ℤ, 0 ≤ a₀ ∧ ∀ a : ℤ, a₀ ≤ a → ∃ h : (tensorObj N ((tensorPullback f).obj (M.tensorPow a.toNat))).IsInvertible, @IsAmple Z (tensorObj N ((tensorPullback f).obj (M.tensorPow a.toNat))) h

reviewed_lean.note: Lean statement isAmple_tensorPullback_tensorPow_of_relative matches the node and Stacks 0892(1) clause by clause: Mathlib QuasiCompact f is equivalent to the affine-preimage condition; relative ampleness is IsAmple of the recorded tensorPullback along (f⁻¹ᵁV).ι for every affine V, the same form as the landed citer QuasiprojectiveQCComposition; IsAmple T M; ∃ a₀:ℤ, 0≤a₀ and ∀ a≥a₀, IsAmple of tensorObj N (tensorPullback f (M.tensorPow a.toNat)); toNat is exact because a≥0; IsInvertible is a Prop that IsAmple's body does not use, so the ∃ h witnesses carry no data. No extra assumptions or universe restriction. Tensor/pullback/IsAmple are the recorded definitions with the same monoidal instance as IsAmple. Only the lean field differs from live; the statement is verbatim. Docstrings have the source place, the blueprint tag and all 8 proof steps; sorry only; all imports exist; report sections present. Edge cases: empty Z or T, empty affine V, a=0, negative a. No findings; no compile, since nothing was changed.
